conn_none_safety.summary: In v2-only mode conn=None. _handle_unchanged (called at runner.py 818 and 867) would crash if reached with conn=None (transaction(None) -> None.commit()). However this path is UNREACHABLE in v2-only mode: (a) fast-reuse path blocked because admission._legacy_gate returns 'legacy_gate:no-current-config-row' when existing_ctx is empty (always empty in v2-only mode, since existing_by_context only populated under _legacy_compat at runner.py 602-604), causing attempt_fast_reuse to return None; (b) unchanged path never hit because _check_and_parse_unit Tier1/Tier2 require file_path in existing_files (empty in v2-only mode), so it always falls through to Tier3 parse returning 'updated'. Empirically verified: fresh index + re-index in v2-only mode both complete without crash.

findings: LATENT FRAGILITY (not a live M5 defect, no must-fix): _handle_unchanged (runner.py lines 818, 867) is invoked with conn=None in v2-only mode IF reached, and transaction(None) would raise AttributeError. Currently unreachable because (a) admission._legacy_gate (admission.py 256-270) returns 'legacy_gate:no-current-config-row' when existing_ctx is empty (always empty in v2-only mode), forcing attempt_fast_reuse to return None; (b) _check_and_parse_unit Tier1/Tier2 require existing_files (empty in v2-only mode), so it always returns 'updated'. Recommend adding an early 'if conn is None: return no-op result' guard in _handle_unchanged for defensive robustness, but this does NOT block M5 because the path is never executed in normal/default operation.

FUNCTIONAL GAP (not an M5 contract violation): v2-only default mode has NO incremental indexing. The v2 admission fast-reuse path (Slice-4A, admission.attempt_fast_reuse) depends on _legacy_gate which requires legacy file-hash rows (existing_ctx populated only under _legacy_compat at runner.py 602-604). In v2-only mode existing_ctx is always empty, so admission always misses and every TU is re-parsed on every re-index. This is a performance characteristic (re-parse all TUs on re-index), not a correctness/semantic defect: normal v2-only operation produces correct v2 semantic storage and no legacy storage is touched. M5 contract does not mandate incremental-indexing performance. Empirically verified: re-index of unchanged project in v2-only mode completes correctly (same config_hash, no crash).

TEST COVERAGE GAP: runtime test C32 only performs a FRESH index in a temp dir (no prior v2 store, so admission returns None at v2_path.exists() check). C32 does not exercise the contract §18 'reindex' step in v2-only mode. I empirically reproduced fresh-index + re-index in v2-only default mode and confirmed no crash and correct config_hash stability, but the gate test suite itself does not cover this path.

OBSERVATION: contract §22 'Fresh Verifier attack plan' lists several attack vectors (remove legacy DB, make legacy DB path unwritable, force legacy helper failure, upgrade from pre-M5 storage). C33 covers the env-opt-in legacy path. The scanner + self-tests (S1-S8) cover forged status / hidden mirror / hidden fallback / legacy postprocess / shared-state premature deletion / pinned World deletion / current World deletion / stale verifier. These passed.

conclusion: After independent reconstruction from current code (not ledgers), I could NOT disprove M5 completion. Normal/default operation is v2-only: no legacy DB opened/written/created/postprocessed/consulted in default mode (conn=None, all legacy calls gated behind _legacy_compat which is False by default). v2 certify/publication/binding/finalization is the sole semantic path and runs by default. v2 lifecycle authority (active/failed/retained/retired/superseded/unfinalized) is owned by the v2 store. GC is reachability-based (ANALYZE/APPLY/VERIFY), pin-protected, shared-state-refcount-checked, no age-only GC. M3B and M4 regressions pass. All 8 self-tests and 7 runtime tests pass. Two non-blocking observations (latent conn=None fragility in _handle_unchanged; no incremental indexing in v2-only mode due to admission's legacy-gate dependency) are noted as findings but are not M5 contract violations — normal/default operation is correct and legacy-free.
